story: 'Bill Gates' 11 rules' (written by Charles J. Sykes)
verification_note: Checked against the cited pages on 2026-10-17. Snopes pages return HTTP 402 to our fetcher; the Snopes 2000 debunk is taken as relayed by AFP. The salary-figure variant ($40,000 vs $60,000) mentioned in our brief could not be confirmed by any fact-check, so it is NOT seeded. The real author is modelled as an established Source (not a Claim), so a version re-attributed to him is recognised as a correction.

claims.text: Bill Gates wrote a list of rules that kids will not learn in school, beginning 'Life is not fair; get used to it.'
claims.evidence: Tes (2008-07-04): the list has circulated online for over a decade. AFP via BOOM (2020-02-24): the Gates attribution has been around for at least 20 years; one of the first debunks was by Snopes in 2000.

claims.text: Bill Gates gave a speech to high school students listing 11 rules they will not learn in school, starting with 'Life is not fair; get used to it.'
claims.evidence: Tes (2008-07-04): a Daily Mail columnist attributed a 'recent speech to American high school pupils' to Bill Gates and reprinted 11 rules. AFP via BOOM (2020-02-24) checks the claim that Gates delivered the rules in a high school speech.

claims.text: Bill Gates said: 'Be nice to nerds. Chances are you'll end up working for one.'
claims.evidence: Check Your Fact (2019-08-30) checks this single line attributed to Gates; Sykes confirmed to the DCNF that the quote originated with him, and his book has 'Be nice to nerds. You may end up working for them.'

sightings.date_note: CONFLICT: Tes (2008) says the list had circulated online 'for over a decade' (so by 1998); AFP (2020) says 'at least 20 years', with Snopes debunking it in 2000.
sightings.snippet: Forwarded email and web posts presenting the rules list as written by Bill Gates.

sightings.date_note: On or before 2008-07-04 (date of the Tes article). Tes names the columnist; the original column URL is not held.
sightings.snippet: Newspaper column reprinting 11 rules as a recent Bill Gates speech to American high school pupils.

sightings.date_note: On or before 2019-08-30 (date of the Check Your Fact article).
sightings.snippet: Social media posts quoting the 'be nice to nerds' line as Bill Gates.

mutations.before_text: a list of rules written by Bill Gates
mutations.after_text: 11 rules delivered by Bill Gates in a speech to high school students
mutations.note: Adds an invented speech. No enum type fits exactly; 'exaggeration' is the closest. Flagged for owner review in DECISIONS.md.

mutations.before_text: a full list of rules for students
mutations.after_text: one line from the list, quoted alone
mutations.note: A truncated list: one rule quoted on its own. context_stripped is best-effort.

origins.note: AFP: the list is by US author Charles J. Sykes (first on his Milwaukee radio show; in his 1995 book 'Dumbing Down Our Kids' and his 2007 book '50 Rules Kids Won't Learn in School'). CONFLICT on first publication: Tes (2008) says a 1996 San Diego Union-Tribune article.

fact_checks.summary: One of the first debunks (2000): the list did not come from Bill Gates. Page not readable by our fetcher; finding relayed by AFP.
Gates was in no way involved in creating the list; its author is Charles J. Sykes.
The 'speech' is a notorious urban myth; the list is Charles J. Sykes's.
Sykes confirmed the quote originated with him, not Gates. (Rating label not read directly; conclusion per the article as relayed in search results.)
